newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - Aug 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - Aug 4.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Australia's 20 biggest unions have lost more than 86,000 members in the past two years, despite a costly recruitment and organisation drive by the Australian Council of Trade Unions aimed at increasing membership by 200,000 by July 1997. Only four of the top 20 recorded any growth in membership between 1994-95 and 1996-97. Page 1.

The United Nations has revealed an international push to maintain greenhouse gas emissions targets, despite protests by nations like Australia. It has also been reported that Japan, a nation Australia was depending on for support, is moving towards uniform targets. Page 3.

Federal Cabinet will be briefed tomorrow by two of Australia's leading jobs experts, Judith Sloan from the National Institute of Labour Studies, and Peter Dawkins from the Melbourne Institute of Applied Economic and Social Research. The briefings come just days before the release of figures expected to show an increase in unemployment. Page 3.

A survey by research company www.consult has revealed while about 1.4 million people have access to the Internet in Australia, many are not impressed by what they see. According to the research, users are getting turned off using the Net as a result of high costs and slow speeds, and rated shopping and financial transactions as their lowest priorities. Page 5.
THE AUSTRALIAN

As more than 600 workers carried on their search for 10 people still buried in the rubble of Wednesday night's landslide at Thredbo, lone survivor Stuart Diver has thanked his rescuers, and all the people around the nation that prayed for him. Diver was moved out of intensive care at the Canberra Hospital last night. Page 1.

Thredbo landslide survivor Stuart Diver is reported to have said to his rescuers "that sky looks fantastic" as he was pulled from the 'concrete tomb' he had been trapped in for 65 hours. During his three-day fight for life, Diver was almost drowned in a flood of running water and was forced to lie in freezing conditions. Page 3.

For the 300 permanent residents of Thredbo village, Saturday was one of the longest days of the year. They were told at 5:37am that contact had been made with a man who was still alive in the ruins of the Bimbadeen staff lodge, and they waited 11 hours before they saw Stuart Diver pulled from the place he had been lying for 65 hours. Page 3.

The South Australian Government has risked a Green backlash at the next election by allowing gas exploration by oil and gas producer Santos in the Coongie Lakes area. The Lakes area is a known habitat for more than 100 species of birdlife and fish, and green groups are pushing the issue as a test of the Government's commitment to the environment and its election promises. Page 3.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Thredbo survivor Stuart Diver kept himself alive for 65 hours in a muddy, freezing and cramped space by dreaming in a semi-conscious state. Diver was joined by rescuer Paul Featherstone early on Saturday morning when he was discovered but previous to that laid next to his wife, Sally, who he had tried to keep above rising waters, but who probably died instantly. Page 1.

A leaked draft submission has outlined how Federal Schools, Vocational Education and Training Minister David Kemp will ask Cabinet for a A$140 million boost to the education system. The extra money is needed because of an influx of teenagers into schools who can no longer get the dole. Page 1.

Rescuers at the site of the Thredbo landslide are racing against a predicted mid-week weather change which could throw their efforts into turmoil. Workers dug through more than 24 metres of rubble at the site yesterday where they found nine people dead and one survivor. Page 1.

Australia has participated in a milestone event where an HIV positive man was injected with healthy cells from his identical twin. This was Australia's first clinical trial of potential gene therapy for HIV and is part of a continuing program in Sydney. Page 6.
THE AGE

Just one day after being rescued from the ruins of the two collapsed ski lodges at Thredbo village, Victorian ski instructor Stuart Diver has invited the media to his hospital bed to thank emergency crews and others for their help. Rescue workers and medical personnel are thrilled and surprised at the way Diver has come through the ordeal of being trapped. Page 1.

Thredbo rescue site commander, police superintendent Charlie Sanderson, has revealed a weather front is expected on Thursday that may hinder the efforts of the rescue teams trying to locate the 10 people still missing in the Thredbo landslide. Sanderson says there is no guarantee that the rescue operations will be completed by Thursday, but says the teams are working as fast as they can. Page A3.

The Australian housing market has seen another rush as interest rates dropped for the fifth time in a year. Combined with the low levels of property available this winter and huge demand, experts say the rush on housing is unlikely to die down before the spring. Page A6.

Federal Environment Minister Robert Hill says he doubts Japan will give researched figures for their proposed greenhouse gas targets compromise, despite their threat to do so. The move by Japan coincides with a general move within the United Nations against Australia's preference for modified gas emissions targets. Page A6.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
